To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the social mobility and the individual life course are not the same.

the social and economic reforms of the 199os in Estonia have had a strong impact on non-Estonians, but this impact was not so much a matter of individual planning or adaptation but rather of structural conditions.
non-Estonian graduates of the 1980s were able to adapt to new conditions, but their adaptation was limited by unfavourable structural changes and institutional constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of the individual’s biography and the structural conditions.
the question of the extent to which structural changes and individual agency are intertwined.

the question whether the post-socialist transformation has brought about a new social order and new social stratification or whether the old order has been preserved and the old stratification has been reproduced.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the social mobility of non-Estonian graduates of 1983 was rather low, but it was not the result of a conscious choice.
the social and cultural resources of non-Estonian “winners” were not sufficient for them to achieve a high social status.
non-Estonian “winners” of the late Soviet period did not succeed in converting their resources gained in the late 1970s and 1980s into other types of social capital in the 1990-2000 period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
non-Estonian destinies were not so much a matter of individual planning but rather a question of adapting oneself to the new circumstances.

the social mobility and individual planning of non-Estonian graduates of the late 198os and early 1990’s were not so much determined by the individual choices and plans as by structural changes and institutional conditions of the labour market.
the social and cultural capital accumulated in the old system was converted into other types of resources, but not in a straightforward way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social and institutional context is of crucial importance for understanding the life trajectories of the post-socialist generation.
the structural changes of the 1999s in the Estonian economy were accompanied by the adaptation of the individual destinies of non- Estonians.
non-Estionians’ personal destinies are not only a result of individual decisions, but also of structural changes in the society.
